question: Extend the sponsor mortality panel to all Form 990 filers answering yes on Part IV line 6 / Schedule D Part I (2011-2025 e-file XML), not just the DAFRC vetted list, so excluded sponsors such as SDG Impact Fund are visible
conclusion_affected: Provider mortality base rate; sponsor-integrity monitoring
rationale: SDG Impact Fund filed $10.1bn of Schedule D DAF value (FY2021-22) and is absent from DAFRC in every year; DAFRC-based mortality cannot see it

question: For the 58 tier-B sponsors that still file Form 990 but stopped reporting DAFs, determine whether DAF balances were granted out, transferred to another sponsor, or reclassified (designated/agency funds), using Schedule D narrative, Schedule O and audited statements
conclusion_affected: Central vs upper exit-rate bound (1.20% vs 1.48%/yr); donor-asset outcomes on exit
rationale: Tier B is the largest outcome group and mixes true DAF exits with reporting changes (e.g. Give2Asia text still describes DAFs with no Sch D Part I)

question: Quantify DAFRC processing gaps: how many sponsors DAFRC marks closed or imputes that still file 990s reporting DAFs (e.g. Donors Fund Inc 6,290 DAFs / $315.8m in FY2024) and what this does to published FY2023-24 totals
conclusion_affected: Market size and sponsor counts in DAFRC FY2024 (30% imputed)
rationale: 15 of 100 exit candidates are artefacts; artefacts concentrate in the top-25 by assets (7 of 25)

question: Re-run mortality when FY2024-FY2025 Schedule D filings are fully processed to measure exits right-censored in this panel (699 EINs whose FY2024 row is imputed)
rationale: FY2024 exits are unobservable; the FY2023 rise may be partly late-filing vintage effects

question: Build a successor-sponsor flow table from Schedule N of every terminated DAF sponsor (2011-2025): which sponsors absorb exiting DAF programs (Fidelity, Schwab, RCF, United Charitable, local CFs) and at what values
conclusion_affected: Consolidator thesis; where donor assets go when a sponsor exits
rationale: All 11 verified ceased sponsors named a transferee; JRCF ($1.32bn) went to Fidelity/Schwab/Dechomai/Vanguard and TIAA Charitable ($138m) to RCF

question: Why did Jasper Ridge Charitable Fund terminate its $1.4bn DAF program in FY2022 and file a 990-PF for 2023 (structure change, adviser decision, regulatory)? Check its 990-PF, Schedule O and any public statements
conclusion_affected: Asset-weighted exit rate (one case is 79-89% of verified exit assets)
rationale: Single exit drives the asset-weighted rate; cause unknown

question: Measure true de novo sponsor formation 2015-2025 (new EIN ruling within 1 year of first Schedule D DAF report) vs coverage additions, by subtype, to set an entrant base rate comparable to the 1.2%/yr exit rate
conclusion_affected: Net formation of sponsors; entrant crowding
rationale: Only 38 of 253 DAFRC entrants FY2020-24 were newly ruled organisations (~0.5%/yr); 201 were existing organisations new to the panel
